title: Can plus one hundred show numbers the others cannot?
description: A calculator in the Land of Tens has only a plus one hundred button. The video finds the presses for many numbers by dividing by one hundred, and then tests the claim that it can show numbers the other two calculators cannot. Keeko raises a hand, thinking that ten thousand needs ten presses.
teaching_notes: One idea: with a button that adds one hundred, the presses are the number divided by one hundred, and every multiple of one hundred is also a multiple of ten. Ask the class to name one number that plus ten cannot show but plus one hundred can. Watch for students who give ten presses for ten thousand, copying the plus one thousand button.

source: Handy Hundreds only has a +100 button. How many times should it be pressed to show: (a) 400, (b) 3,700, (c) 10,000, (d) 53,000, (e) 90,000, (f) 97,600, (g) 1,00,000, (h) the number shown by 582 presses, (i) the hundreds in ten thousand, (j) the hundreds in one lakh; (k) Handy Hundreds says there are some numbers which Tedious Tens and Thoughtful Thousands can't show but it can: is this true?
video_script.why: The child has counted presses for the plus one thousand and plus ten buttons and now meets the button in between.
video_script.substitution: A button that adds one hundred is pressed as many times as there are hundreds in the number, and every multiple of one hundred is also a multiple of ten.
video_script.anchor: A calculator has only a plus one hundred button: can it show numbers that the plus ten and plus one thousand calculators cannot?
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko uses the ten presses of the plus one thousand button for ten thousand. This button adds one hundred, so ten thousand holds one hundred hundreds and needs one hundred presses.
video_script.payoff_line: Tedious Tens can show every number that Handy Hundreds can

final_answer.spoken: Tedious Tens can show every number that Handy Hundreds can

hold_back: Tedious Tens can show every number
maths_rules: (h) 582 × 100 = 58,200; (i) ten thousand holds 100 hundreds; (j) one lakh holds 1000 hundreds
(k) every multiple of 100 is a multiple of 10, so Tedious Tens shows every number Handy Hundreds shows; the statement is not true. Thoughtful Thousands alone cannot show 400
video_script.design: One idea: presses of a plus one hundred button are the number divided by one hundred, and its numbers are also reachable with plus ten. Wrong idea: Keeko gives ten thousand only ten presses. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the presses for many numbers. Then we decide whether the claim is true.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, divide each number by one hundred. Four hundred needs four presses, and three thousand seven hundred needs thirty seven.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Ten thousand needs one hundred presses.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, fifty three thousand needs five hundred thirty presses, and ninety thousand needs nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Ninety seven thousand six hundred needs nine hundred seventy six presses.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>One lakh needs one thousand presses.

marks.m2: the hundreds in ten thousand and in one lakh are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, five hundred eighty two presses add five hundred eighty two hundreds. That is fifty eight thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Ten thousand holds one hundred hundreds, and one lakh holds one thousand hundreds.

beats.on_screen: Answer: every multiple of 100 is a multiple of 10, so the claim is not true

marks.m1: the strip shows the multiples of 100 inside the multiples of 10

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Thoughtful Thousands cannot show four hundred, but the plus ten calculator can. Every multiple of one hundred is also a multiple of ten.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Tedious Tens can show every number that Handy Hundreds can.
